title: Onboarding Microlearning & Competency Rubric: Sprint-Based New Hire Path
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview:
This playbook defines Redwood Inference's microlearning-based onboarding sprint approach and a companion competency rubric for assessing new hire readiness across engineering and product-adjacent roles. It is intended to standardize manager expectations, shorten time-to-impact, and create objective, coachable milestones tied to hiring evidence and early performance conversations.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: Individual contributors (IC) and first-line managers across Engineering, Product, and Developer Experience.
- Audience: hiring managers, people-ops partners, onboarding buddies, hiring panel members, and team leads responsible for 0–90 day programs.

Goals and success metrics:
- Ramp time: median ‘able-to-own-feature’ reduced from 12 to 9 weeks within 6 months of roll-out.
- Competency coverage: 90% of new hires should score "meets expectations" or above on core rubric by week 12.
- Manager satisfaction: > 80% managers rate the playbook as useful in quarterly survey.

Design principles:
1) Microlearning first: short, focused modules (10–45 minutes) that can be completed asynchronously.
2) Evidence over ceremony: require small artifacts or checkpoints (PR, doc, demo) not passive completion.
3) Manager-enabled, not manager-heavy: provide templates so managers can coach in 1:1 with minimal prep.
4) Cross-functional onboarding: early customer/product context for engineers; early infra/ops basics for product managers.

Core components (what to expect):
- Microlearning module catalog: short modules with owner, estimated time, and acceptance evidence.
- 14-day sprints: 4 sprints (0–2, 3–4, 5–8, 9–12 weeks) with prioritized learning objectives and artifacts.
- Competency rubric: mapped to hire bands (IC2–IC4) and role families.
- Manager checklist and 1:1 conversation templates.
- Hiring feedback integration: how hiring notes map to initial sprint goals.

Microlearning module catalog (example):
| Module ID | Title | Owner | Time | Acceptance evidence | When recommended |
| ML-01 | Product & Mission Primer | People-Ops / Growth | 20m | Written 3-bullet summary + manager sign-off | Week 0–1 |
| ML-02 | Security & Data Handling at Redwood | Security | 30m | Acknowledgment + 1-sentence example of data flow concern | Week 0–1 |
| ML-03 | Local Dev Environment: Start-to-First-PR | Eng DX | 45m | Merge of a starter PR that runs unit tests | Week 0–2 |
| ML-04 | Serving Runtime Overview | Eng Serving Runtime | 30m | 10-minute demo + 1 Q/A note | Week 1–3 |
| ML-05 | Observability & Tracing Basics | Eng Platform | 25m | Create one trace in staging and link in ticket | Week 2–4 |

Sprint structure (recommended cadence):
- Sprint 0–2 (Orientation sprint — weeks 0–2)
  1. Complete ML-01, ML-02, ML-03.
  2. Deliverables: 3-bullet product summary (ML-01), security acknowledgment (ML-02), PR merged (ML-03).
  3. Manager check-in: 30 minutes end of week 2; use "Orientation 1:1" template below.
- Sprint 3–4 (Customer & Tooling — weeks 3–4)
  1. Complete ML-04, ML-05.
  2. Deliverables: demo of a runtime flow, link to created trace.
  3. Manager check-in: 30 minutes end of week 4; evaluate early competency with rubric.
- Sprint 5–8 (Ownership & Delivery — weeks 5–8)
  1. Focus on a small, scoped ticket with cross-team impact.
  2. Deliverable: feature PR + design note + 10-minute demo.
  3. Manager check-in and peer feedback collected.
- Sprint 9–12 (Independence & Quality — weeks 9–12)
  1. Deliverable: owner-of-record on a minor feature or an infrastructure improvement.
  2. Final readiness review using the competency rubric.

Manager responsibilities (checklist):
- Pre-start: review hiring notes, map 3 initial sprint goals, assign buddy.
- Day 1–7: ensure access, schedule orientation, confirm ML module assignments.
- Weekly: 30-minute structured 1:1 using templates; log evidence artifacts to onboarding tracker.
- Week 4 and week 12: perform rubric assessments and upload to the HR LMS.

1:1 conversation templates (short):
- Orientation 1:1 (end of week 2):
  - What surprised you in your first two weeks?
  - Which microlearning felt most useful? Which was unclear?
  - Confirm next sprint deliverables and support needed.
- Competency checkpoint (week 4):
  - Review artifacts from sprints 0–4.
  - Based on the rubric, which 1–2 skills need focus?
  - Agree on measurable action (pairing sessions or shadowing).

Competency rubric (sample criteria and scoring):
- Scoring legend: 1 = Needs support; 2 = Developing; 3 = Meets expectations; 4 = Exceeds expectations.
- Core categories (apply to IC engineering roles):
  1. Product context & customer empathy
  2. Dev environment & velocity (can land safe PRs)
  3. System-level understanding (service boundaries, latency/cost tradeoffs)
  4. Quality & observability (tests, traces, runbook updates)
  5. Collaboration & cross-team communication

Sample rubric table (compact):
| Category | Week 4 target (IC2) | Week 12 target (IC2) | Evidence examples |
| Product context | 2 | 3 | 3-bullet summary, customer ticket review |
| Dev velocity | 2 | 3 | Merged PRs with passing CI, simple fix without revert |
| System understanding | 1 | 3 | Diagram in design doc, ability to explain runtime flow |
| Quality & observability | 2 | 3 | Tests added, staging trace present, runbook contribution |
| Collaboration | 2 | 3 | Peer feedback, cross-team ticket ownership |

Scoring process and thresholds:
- Week 4 checkpoint: if two or more categories are scored 1, open an individualized support plan (ISP) with clear actions and owners.
- Week 12 readiness: at least 4 categories must be >= 3 to be considered "independent contributor (meets expectations)".

Evidence requirements and storage:
- All acceptance evidence (PR links, demo notes, trace links) must be attached to the onboarding tracker ticket in Jira and summarized in the new hire’s onboarding doc in Confluence.
- People-Ops will extract anonymized roll-up metrics monthly.

Hiring panel tie-ins (how hiring notes feed onboarding):
1. The hiring manager transcribes 3 evidence-backed strengths and 1–2 coached development areas from the final interview packet into the onboarding plan within 48 hours of offer acceptance.
2. These become sprint goals with visible owner and measurement (e.g., pair session, specific PR).
3. If the hiring panel rated a candidate as "high potential but limited infra exposure", schedule additional ML infra pairings in sprint 3–4.

Individualized Support Plan (ISP) workflow (when triggered):
1. Trigger: Week 4 rubric shows two or more categories at score 1, or manager raises concern.
2. Owner: hiring manager + people-ops L&D partner.
3. Steps:
  a. 3-day intake meeting to set 30/60/90 day goals.
  b. Assign mentor and weekly focused sessions (30–60m).
  c. Define measurable checkpoints; re-assess after 30 days.
  d. If insufficient progress after 60 days, escalate to people-ops for role fit conversation.

Manager calibration and training:
- Frequency: quarterly 60-minute calibration for new-hire assessments.
- Agenda: sample rubric reviews, ISP case studies, scoring alignment exercises.
- Deliverable: calibrated scoring guide and exemplar evidence samples in the manager playbook.

Operational integrations and tooling:
- Onboarding tracker: Jira project key ONB.
- Evidence repository: Confluence space /confluence/people-ops/onboarding-evidence.
- LMS tags: microlearning modules use tag "ML-2026" for roll-up reporting.
- HR sync: LMS and HRIS weekly sync to import completion signals.

Template artifacts (copyable snippets):
- Sprint goal line: "Sprint 0–2: Become familiar with product mission and land first PR. Evidence: confluence link + PR link."
- Manager note line: "Week 4 rubric result: [category:x score], actions: [pairing1, doc revision], owner: [name], due: [date]"

Rollout plan and timeline (recommended):
1. Pilot cohort (Q2 2026): 10 new hires across Eng and Product; collect qualitative feedback.
2. Revise modules & rubric (Q3 2026): integrate pilot feedback and create manager calibration materials.
3. Company-wide launch (Q4 2026): enable all hiring managers; run first quarterly calibration.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Manager time burden. Mitigation: pre-built templates and recommended 30-minute weekly cadence.
- Risk: Passive completion. Mitigation: require artifact evidence and manager sign-off.
- Risk: Inconsistent scoring across teams. Mitigation: quarterly calibration and exemplar evidence library.

Appendices:
A. Sample onboarding sprint schedule (week-by-week)
  - Week 0: Pre-boarding checklist completed by manager and IT.
  - Day 1: Orientation, ML-01, system access, buddy intro.
  - Week 1: ML-02, ML-03; schedule first walkthrough with service owner.
  - Week 2–3: ML-04; first small PR.
  - Week 4: Competency checkpoint, manager upload.
  - Week 6–8: Ownership PR and cross-team demo.
  - Week 12: Final readiness review and feedback cycle kickoff.
